summary: Same idea — a pulsing heart on the grid filled with a vertical rainbow gradient — but the port draws the heart UPSIDE DOWN (apex up, lobes down) and decouples the hue sweep from the beat, where the original completes exactly one full rainbow per heartbeat.
observations: Both sides render cleanly on the default 16x16 grid rig with no compile or runtime errors, neither binds sensors, and both are steady over 240 s (brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 1 = the t=0 artefact only). Survey at 60 s and 240 s shows a single regime on both sides — no mode rotation.

STRUCTURE — the port's heart is vertically mirrored. At 48x48 (label grid48) the original draws a textbook heart: two rounded lobes at the top with a cleft between them, tapering to a single point at the bottom. The port draws the same silhouette rotated/flipped so the point is at the TOP and the two rounded lobes are at the BOTTOM. Confirmed numerically on the default rig: a --dump at t=3.25 s and t=3.75 s (label dump-shape) shows the original's lit rows spanning 1-13 with the cleft in its top row, and the port's spanning 4-12 with the cleft in its bottom row; flipping the port's frame top-to-bottom recovers essentially the original's silhouette. Lit-pixel centroid row: orig 6.05-6.70, port 8.32-9.04 (16 rows), i.e. the mirror of each other.

STRUCTURE — the port's heart is smaller and sits lower. Lit pixel count over one beat at 16x16: orig 80-130 px, port 62-108 px. The original stays inside cols 1-14; the port reaches cols 0-15 (touching the grid edge) at its peak. Pulse depth is comparable (orig max/min area 1.63, port 1.74).

MOTION — beat rate. Untouched, the original's pulse period is 1.30 s (26 frames at 20 fps, autocorrelation of meanBrightness) and the port's is 1.05 s (21 frames) — the port beats ~24% too fast. Both are fps-invariant: re-rendering at 10 / 20 / 40 fps gives orig 1.30 s and port 1.00-1.05 s at every rate, so there is no frame-rate coupling on either side.

COLOR — the hue gradient down the shape matches exactly. Circular-mean hue per row (dump-shape, 16x16) advances +12 deg per row on BOTH sides, in the same screen direction (top of grid = lower hue). Because the port's silhouette is flipped, this means the gradient runs lobes-to-apex on the original and apex-to-lobes on the port.

COLOR — the hue-vs-beat relationship is the second major divergence. The original's hue advances ~276 deg/s, i.e. a full 360 deg rainbow in 1.304 s, which is its heartbeat period: every beat sweeps the whole rainbow once and the colour resets in step with the pulse. The port's hue advances ~110 deg/s (a full rainbow every ~3.2 s), so its colour drifts across roughly three beats and consecutive beats look nearly the same colour. This holds untouched (label long40) and with the beat dialed to match (label dialed-hue): sliderBeatRate changes the pulse rate but leaves the hue rate unchanged.

BRIGHTNESS — the port is dimmer. Over 40 s: orig meanBrightness avg 44.4 (min 25, max 57), port avg 34.4 (min 13, max 50). Most of this follows from the port's smaller lit area; peak per-channel means are comparable (orig meanR max 94 / meanB max 115, port 94 on all three channels).

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH — the original exposes NO controls at all (meta.json sides.orig.controls is empty). The port adds two sliders the original does not have: sliderAntialias (label 'Antialias') and sliderBeatRate (label 'BeatRate'). Both are genuinely live in the probe (maxDelta 12.04 / 11.02, maxDeltaLit 36.05 / 29.22) and in manual sweeps.
The pattern is not random-driven: seed 1234 renders identically to seed 1 on both sides (label seed1234, same stats as baseline).
Both sides are resolution-independent: the same heart figure appears at 8x8, 16x16 and 48x48, just coarser or finer, with no change in feature count.

dials.name: sliderAntialias
dials.origEffect: control absent on the original — it exposes no controls at all
dials.portEffect: live: edge softness of the heart. At 0 the silhouette has hard, fully-lit edges (port meanBrightness avg 41 over 12 s); at 0.5 the edge is feathered over ~1 px (avg 31); at 1 the edge is heavily blurred and the whole shape dims (avg 22). The untouched default sits near the 0.35-0.5 look, which is close to the original's own edge softness (both sides show intermediate-brightness edge pixels in --dump).

dials.name: sliderBeatRate
dials.origEffect: control absent on the original — its pulse period is fixed at 1.30 s
dials.portEffect: live: pulse period. 0 -> ~0.32 s (6-7 frames at 20 fps), 0.5 -> ~1.48 s, 1 -> ~2.55 s, untouched -> 1.05 s. Setting it to ~0.44 reproduces the original's 1.30 s period (measured 26.7 frames, label dialed-match). It does NOT affect the hue sweep rate.

feedback: Flip the heart vertically. The port currently draws it apex-up with the two lobes at the bottom of the grid; the original is lobes-up with the apex at the bottom. This is the single most visible difference — obvious at any grid size, unmistakable at 48x48. Everything else about the silhouette (lobe roundness, cleft depth, taper) already matches once the port's frame is mirrored top-to-bottom.

Lock the hue sweep to the heartbeat. The original advances hue at ~276 deg/s so that exactly one full rainbow completes per 1.30 s beat — colour and pulse are phase-locked and the colour visibly resets on every beat. The port advances hue at ~110 deg/s (one rainbow per ~3.2 s, about three beats), so its colour crawls and successive beats read as the same colour. Make the hue rate derive from the beat period rather than being an independent constant.

Slow the default pulse from 1.05 s to 1.30 s (about 24% slower). The port's sliderBeatRate already spans this range — 0.44 lands on 1.30 s — so the fix can be as simple as moving the untouched default.

Grow the heart slightly and re-centre it. At 16x16 the original occupies 80-130 lit px inside cols 1-14 across a beat; the port occupies 62-108 px and reaches cols 0-15 at peak. The port is both smaller in area and pushed against the grid edge horizontally at its largest — aim for the original's footprint, which never touches the outer column.

Drop sliderAntialias and sliderBeatRate, or at least be aware they are additions: the original pattern exposes no controls whatsoever, so any dial on the port is a fidelity gap in the control surface even though both behave sensibly. If they are kept deliberately, their defaults must reproduce the original exactly (see the beat-rate default above); the antialias default is already close.

The vertical hue gradient itself is correct and needs no change: both sides advance +12 deg of hue per grid row in the same screen direction, at full saturation. Preserve that when flipping the shape — the gradient should keep running in the same screen direction (top of grid = lower hue), not be flipped along with the silhouette.
